note: 10 mW ERP (within SRD band limits); OOK (On-Off Keying) with Manchester encoding. Bit period ~604 us. Frame: preamble (hardware sync pulses + software sync) followed by 56 bits (7 bytes) of scrambled data.; Somfy uses EXACTLY 433.42 MHz (NOT 433.92 MHz) for the RTS protocol. Data is Manchester encoded: rising edge = 1, falling edge = 0. 56-bit payload scrambled by XORing each byte with previous scrambled byte. Rolling code is 16 bits wide but receiver acceptance window of ~100 codes means effective entropy is 9-10 bits. Frame structure: wake-up pulses, hardware sync (2 high pulses), software sync (1 long high pulse of ~4550 us), then Manchester-encoded data. Somfy has shipped over 200 million RTS devices worldwide.

application: DME interrogator frequencies. Aircraft DME interrogators transmit in 1025-1150 MHz range (X channel) but many DME ground transponder reply frequencies fall in 962-1024 MHz. This sub-band contains DME transponder replies and some DME interrogator channels.

note: DME interrogator: up to 2 kW peak; Ground transponder: up to 1 kW peak; Gaussian pulse pairs (3.5 us pulse width, 12 us or 30 us spacing for X/Y channels); DME channel scheme: 252 channels (126 X + 126 Y). Interrogator/transponder frequency offset is +63 MHz for X channels 1-63, -63 MHz for X channels 64-126, +63 MHz for Y channels 1-63, -63 MHz for Y channels 64-126. This is uniform worldwide.

application: UAT (Universal Access Transceiver) at 978 MHz. US-only ADS-B alternative to 1090ES, authorized for use below FL180 (18,000 ft). Provides ADS-B Out and FIS-B (weather/TFR) and TIS-B (traffic) services. NOT used outside the US.
typical_devices: Garmin GDL 88 (UAT transceiver), uAvionix skyBeacon/tailBeaconX (UAT), FreeFlight RANGR FYX (UAT), Garmin GDL 52/50 (portable UAT receiver for FIS-B weather); Receivers: Stratux (DIY ADS-B receiver using RTL-SDR at 978+1090), ForeFlight Sentry (UAT+1090 receiver)
source: FAR 14 CFR 91.225/91.227 / TSO-C154c (UAT ADS-B) / RTCA DO-282B (UAT MOPS) / AC 20-165B
note: UAT transceiver: up to 20W (43 dBm) per TSO-C154c; CPM (Continuous Phase Modulation), 1.041667 Mbps, TDM (Time Division Multiplexed) with 1 second frame containing 3200 message slots; 978 MHz UAT is UNIQUE TO THE US. No other country uses UAT. It provides free weather (FIS-B: NEXRAD, METARs, TAFs, TFRs) and traffic information (TIS-B) to GA pilots. Above FL180, only 1090ES is accepted. Approximately 50% of US GA fleet uses UAT rather than 1090ES.
